top_findings.title: MCP server crashes on the notifications/initialized notification — handshake never completes
top_findings.evidence: BrazilianSoccerMcpServer.java:7 — the main read-loop catch block builds Map.of("jsonrpc","2.0","error",...,"id",null); java.util.Map.of rejects null values. notifications/initialized hits the switch default in response() (line 8) and throws IllegalArgumentException, which reaches that catch and NPEs. Reproduced by stdio probe: initialize answered, then NullPointerException at java.util.Map.of(Map.java:1410) <- main(BrazilianSoccerMcpServer.java:7), process exits 1, tools/list left unanswered. Independently corroborated by _factual.json score=0.0 'did not complete the MCP handshake'.
top_findings.suggestion: Reply to JSON-RPC notifications (requests with no id) with nothing, and build error/response objects with a null-tolerant map (HashMap) so a null id does not throw.

top_findings.title: Server process dies on any error input (unknown method/tool, missing required arg) instead of returning a JSON-RPC error
top_findings.evidence: response() default (line 8) and call() default (line 9) throw IllegalArgumentException; required() (line 12) throws on missing args. Every throw reaches the same main catch at line 7 whose Map.of(...,"id",null) NPEs. Reproduced in three separate processes — bogus/method, tools/call name=no_such_tool, and team_statistics with empty arguments — each exits 1 at Map.of(Map.java:1410); a valid team_statistics{team:Flamengo} call by contrast returns correctly, confirming only the error path crashes.
top_findings.suggestion: Construct the JSON-RPC error with a null-tolerant map, echo the request id, and keep the read loop alive after catching a per-request error.
